asr.full_text: isn't familiar with the world of advertisements we all see hundreds of ads in a single day but how many of them capture your attention advertisers go all out merely to get people talking about the advert and associate it with the product agencies and advertising companies actively seek opportunities to get their audience talking especially with promising events for content and advertisers one event that is appealing to advertisers we all know is the super bowl. But, what makes the super bowl so unique Super Bowl has the largest live television audience and is one of the television events where people peculiarly don't skip the ads. While most companies spent eight figure budgets on hiring Hollywood celebrities for a super bowl ad Coinbase took to a multi-color bouncing QR code for 60 seconds. The 1-minute commercial simply had a color shifting QR code bouncing from corner to corner on the television screen, very similar to the DVD video logo bouncing off the corners of the screen. The core idea was to drive participation over just brand awareness. When scanned, the QR code led to the sign-up page offering fifteen dollars in free Bitcoin in exchange for setting up an account by February 15th. What happened next, made history. Very soon, Coinbase became the second most downloaded app on App Store in the U.S. Coinbase also took a well deserved seat on one of the top five discussed brands on twitter on February 14, 2022. The numbers from the campaign looked very promising. According to the data released by Coinbase itself, it had an estimated 20 million scans which was 6 times the project estimate. The approximate number of new customers based on their crypto apps went up to 1.5 million. What followed was not surprising. The estimated revenue of the campaign was $135 million. When scanned, the QR codes at Super Bowl prompted a signup form that collected PII data. Not just that, with the robust QR code solutions such as beaconstack. A brand can capture many more first party data without even prompting a sign up form. Following the precedents set by Coinbase, many other brands squeezed in QR codes in their super bowl ad campaigns. But none were as successful as Coinbase. The primary reason for that is undivided attention to one call to action. QR codes were everywhere at the super bowl one of the most difficult challenges in advertising is measuring the roi it's all the more complicated if the journey is not 100 digital as in the case of tv commercials ooh billboards and newspaper ads qr codes have become a way to bridge the gap in attribution. As a result, many brands during the Superbowl also used QR codes. Rocket Mortgage. The brand squeezed in the promotion of a co-founded brand, StockX, in the same Rocket Mortgage ad. Liquid Death, a canned water company, added a QR code in the last three seconds of the regional ad. The first three users to spot it received an entire pallet of liquid death for one dollar. Let's look at some other brands who did justice to their QR code campaign for TVs. Kanye West QR code ad. Kanye West gave the pattern for a successful QR code campaign in his full-page New York times ad. Burger King QR Code ad. An identical QR code campaign for TV by Burger King took the internet by storm. Want to create your QR code campaign for TV? Check out our video on easy steps to create QR codes on TV. I'll put the link in the description below. The pandemic brought significant shifts and disruptions in how people consume and use QR codes. Almost every restaurant during the pandemic shifted to a contact-less way of serving the menu. Everyone young and old knew how to instantly engage with a QR code. Super Bowl ads in 2022 proved that QR codes are here to stay and are the new way to run measurable campaigns. If you want to learn more about these fantastic QR codes, what else they can do, and which industries are using them, check out the other videos on our channel. textual.observation: The described Coinbase Super Bowl QR campaign directed viewers who scanned the code to a signup page offering fifteen dollars in free Bitcoin in exchange for setting up an account by February 15th.

evidence.quote: When scanned, the QR code led to the sign-up page offering fifteen dollars in free Bitcoin in exchange for setting up an account by February 15th.

textual.context: Presented as analysis of an advertising campaign and its results, rather than as a direct current offer from the video publisher.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised cryptocurrency reward is explicitly linked to scanning and creating an account, with a stated deadline; later review may assess the offer's context and terms.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish whether the offer was still available, whether viewers received Bitcoin, or what account information or conditions were required beyond the stated signup and deadline.

textual.observation: The described Coinbase Super Bowl QR-code signup form collected personally identifiable information during the account-creation flow.

textual.limitations: The records do not identify the specific information collected, how it was used, or whether the statement applies to all viewers or only the described campaign.
